problem_text:
A logistics company must coordinate a fleet of drones to inspect nine critical communication towers scattered across a region.  
The towers are positioned at the following grid coordinates (in kilometers relative to a central hub):  
Tower Alpha: (190,174)  
Tower Beta: (31,132)  
Tower Gamma: (48,9)  
Tower Delta: (200,100)  
Tower Epsilon: (113,95)  
Tower Zeta: (193,48)  
Tower Eta: (116,91)  
Tower Theta: (161,19)  
Tower Iota: (11,10)  

The flight distances between towers (in kilometers) are precisely known:  
Alpha to Gamma: 217.7 km  
Alpha to Delta: 74.7 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 110.3 km  
Alpha to Zeta: 126.0 km  
Alpha to Eta: 111.2 km  
Alpha to Theta: 157.7 km  
Alpha to Iota: 242.8 km  
Beta to Gamma: 124.2 km  
Beta to Delta: 172.0 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 90.0 km  
Beta to Zeta: 182.5 km  
Beta to Eta: 94.4 km  
Beta to Theta: 172.2 km  
Beta to Iota: 123.6 km  
Gamma to Delta: 177.2 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 107.8 km  
Gamma to Zeta: 150.2 km  
Gamma to Eta: 106.5 km  
Gamma to Theta: 113.4 km  
Gamma to Iota: 37.0 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 87.1 km  
Delta to Zeta: 52.5 km  
Delta to Eta: 84.5 km  
Delta to Theta: 89.9 km  
Delta to Iota: 209.3 km  
Epsilon to Zeta: 92.8 km  
Epsilon to Eta: 5.0 km  
Epsilon to Theta: 89.9 km  
Epsilon to Iota: 132.8 km  
Zeta to Eta: 88.2 km  
Zeta to Theta: 43.2 km  
Zeta to Iota: 185.9 km  
Eta to Theta: 84.9 km  
Eta to Iota: 132.6 km  
Theta to Iota: 150.3 km  

Due to airspace restrictions, a direct flight between Tower Alpha and Tower Beta is prohibited.  
Furthermore, exactly one of the following two flight corridors must be incorporated into the inspection circuit: the corridor linking Beta and Gamma, or the corridor linking Gamma and Delta.

The objective is to determine the most efficient closed flight path that visits every tower exactly once and returns to the origin, minimizing the total flight distance.
